_comment: Training COURSES: a pipeline of schools > phases > units laid over the tracks and Library cards that already exist. A unit is a reading (a doc under missiongen/data/courses/), a track (optionally a ride range and a preferred aircraft/era), a card (a Library template, optionally with a preferred aircraft), or a planned unit that says plainly what is not built yet and why. courses.py resolves each unit against the shelf so a course can never claim a ride the Library does not have. Status, prerequisites and the check ride are data here; progress is the student's own browser (nothing is stored server-side).

f4e_pipeline.label: F-4E Phantom II — The Training Pipeline
f4e_pipeline.premise: Learn it, fly it, fight it. From never having started a Phantom to leading a timed strike package: three schools in the order the real pipeline runs them — learn the airplane, fly it to a standard, then fight it. Every ride is generated, graded in-mission where the Mission Editor can see it, and ships with its own brief and kneeboard.
blurb: Most people buy the module and meander through it. That is fine — but
there is a faster way, and it is the one every air force uses: UPT teaches
you to fly an airplane, the FRS teaches you this one, MQT teaches you to
fight it. This pipeline is that order, with the missions attached.

schools.label: Ground School and UPT
schools.intro: Ground school is where you learn the airplane you are going to fly — the history chapter first, because an aircraft's habits come from what it was built to be. Then nothing in this school is about the Phantom in particular: instruments, timing, formation and the tanker are the same problems in every jet, and a pilot who arrives at the FRS already able to hold a position, fly a card on the clock and take gas has half the conversion done. Fly it in the F-4E if you own it; fly it in whatever you own if you do not.

units.label: Aviation basics — the six numbers you fly by
Chapter 0 — The Phantom: where it came from, what it taught

phases.label: Formation
phases.intro: Five stages, each an AI lead you fly on, then the check profile twice: once with the coach on, once in silence. The Library card lets you pick the airframe; the pipeline pre-selects the Phantom.

phases.label: Timing — the clock on the card
Air-to-air refuelling
phases.intro: The boom lane of the Refuelling Academy, generated for the Phantom in the Cold War era. Eleven rides; ten are graded.

units.label: After the check — fuel transfer and the night ride

schools.label: FRS — Know Your Jet
schools.intro: The conversion course. You read where the Phantom came from in ground school; here you fly it. The contact phase, systems, then the squadron checkout flown from the 70th TFS's own 1980 paperwork, and the weapons deliveries from its own planning sheets.

units.label: Instrument recovery — TACAN penetration and ILS to minimums
units.why: Needs a glideslope coach: the Mission Editor can read altitude and DME, so it can be built trigger-only. Next on the roadmap.

units.label: Radar work with Jester — search, lock, sort
units.why: Grading switchology needs the F-4E's cockpit parameters, which are verified only for the radios. The ride can be built uncoached first.

phases.label: Tactical checkout — the White Knights syllabus
phases.intro: Rides 4 to 11 of Squadron Checkout: line abreast, comm-out turns, ridge crossings, threats, the route abort, intercepts, the three-ship and BFM.

phases.label: Weapons — Proud Phantom
phases.intro: The deliveries, from the squadron's own Weapons Information Sheet: LALD, 30-degree dive, high drag, dive toss, then the attacks that put four airplanes on one target.

phases.label: Check ride
phases.intro: The B'NAI attack with no coaching, over the ground it was invented on, with an SA-6 in the mission. Pass this and you are a Phantom pilot.

schools.label: MQT — Fight the Jet
schools.intro: Mission qualification: the airplane is known, now it goes to war. Routed strikes through the gun belt, a timed package, the corridors of the Cold War. The rides here are the ones the rest of the Library was built from.

units.label: Package lead — SEAD and strike on one timeline, four ships
units.why: The campaign engine (chained sorties, carried fuel and clock) is on the roadmap; this is its first mission.

units.label: Night TACAN strike — the Fulda 1979 problem
units.why: Needs the instrument recovery from the FRS first.

f4e_pipeline.tagline: Learn it, fly it, fight it.
